findings.one_line: The cited ordinary commutation lemma requires q to be Markov with respect to the current CADMG, but def:trace-state supplies only a normalized kernel and neither Swap nor legality establishes the Markov invariant; hence the cited conclusion cannot discharge the claimed erased-state/provenance equality. Add and preserve that invariant (and relate pi's divisions to q's factors), or state the lemma conditionally.

The SCM independence calculation can establish the displayed observed functional, but it does not construct the asserted legal colored fixing that produces P(Y|do(A),R_W), identify its fixing denominator/license, or prove that this expression is among TCF's enumerated candidates; the proof instead assumes 'the licensed fixing that derives' it. Exhibit that trace from the definitions before claiming the fix-then-select witness and its restrict-first closure obstruction.

cited_checks.note: The supplied attested Lemma 30 states equality of the two fixing-order graphs and kernels; this matches the node's ordinary CADMG/kernel commutation claim under its stated Markov and fixability hypotheses.
The supplied Tarski--Seidenberg attestation gives a quantifier-free Psi(Y) equivalent to Phi(Y) at every point of the real closed field, exactly matching the node's invocation.

The supplied CAD attestation gives a cylindrical decomposition adapted to every finite polynomial family; together with the attested definitions of decomposition and adaptation, this is the node's finite disjoint sign-invariant semialgebraic cell claim.

The supplied Proposition 4 attestation states that its five conditions identify P(Y|do(A=a)) by the weighted context formula with Theta_r(a) from equation (6), matching the DA4-certificate invocation.
The supplied Theorem 1/equation (3)/Corollary 2 attestation gives identification iff every context graph identifies and the observed-context weighted aggregation, matching the root-control node.
The supplied Theorem 5 attestation says every expression returned by ID for P_x(y) is correct, matching the node's recursive semi-Markovian soundness invocation.
